text:
Jake Evans was a seventh-round pick, 207th overall in 2014, and he has spent his whole NHL career in Montreal. He is the kind of center coaches trust on the penalty kill, and the players who resemble him statistically are killers too.

This season he has 3 goals and 8 points in 21 games on just 16 shots. That is efficient, maybe too efficient: 18.8% shooting sits above his usual range of about 11 to 17, though his 3 goals almost exactly match his 2.9 expected goals (the quality of his chances). His biggest night was Nov. 12 in Boston, when he had two points including the winner, per CBS Sports.

The five-on-five numbers are a pleasant surprise. Montreal takes 54.3% of the expected goals with him on the ice, 5 points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, so that is a change worth tracking.

His role has grown lately: 16.4 minutes a night over his last ten games, above his season average. Watch whether the bigger minutes keep the team's share of play on his side.
